voice_direction: Warm, clear English product narration. Sound composed and conversational, with precise emphasis on evidence, changing recommendations and human review. Keep the measured spoken pace natural; the shortened script leaves a short scene-boundary pause. Pronounce Fraud Loop and Tiger Graph as two words, MCP as M C P, and GraphRAG as Graph Rag. Read percentages and approval levels naturally. Do not read scene identifiers or durations aloud.

scenes.text: Fraud Loop investigates fraud alerts using Tiger Graph evidence, historical cases, explicit policy, and human review.
The queue shows verdicts and approvals. Twenty saved cases include nine fraud, eight legitimate and three uncertain outcomes. Two recommend reports. All twenty have passed validation.
Case fourteen begins with a shared device alert. Its trigger, transactions, evidence and timeline stay together in one review.
This local graph spans twenty-six transactions and twenty card groups. Exposure is nearly thirty-eight hundred dollars. Nine card identities remain unresolved.
Related signals are capped. Device sharing alone cannot prove fraud. This score is an evidence heuristic.
Read confirmed historical outcomes and analyst notes. These older saved answers label missing retrieval rankings rather than inventing them.
Here, policy recommends a card block and report, both requiring level two approval. Both sets of actions stay visible. No card was blocked or report filed.
A simulated customer confirmation clears case two. Suspicion falls from about forty-three percent to four percent. The final recommendation closes the alert, with zero exposure.
This local simulator streams historical transactions. A lowered demo threshold opens a review. The alert score does not decide fraud.
Each alert links to a case. The limits: five transactions per second, one active review and ten waiting.
When authorization is unclear, the agent saves its assessment and pauses. The request states what evidence is needed and why.
The demo analyst records a customer denial, with a level one role and timestamp. In this demo, no actual customer was contacted.
The denial changes uncertain to fraud: seventy point two to ninety-six percent. Case creation is automatic; blocking needs level one approval for this case.
Graph Rag controls index weights, time windows and evidence counts. Each case keeps its settings, even while waiting for human evidence.
Rank fusion blends available vector, graph and text matches. This local view shows each source's role; missing scores stay missing.
Inspect the exact evidence brief. Policy owns the verdict and actions. This preview calls no language model; the demo used templates.
Viewers inspect; reviewers see their allowed controls. Decisions have an audit trail. These local demo roles are not bank authentication.
Bank history stays apart from agent memory. Each case uses only earlier evidence, so future facts stay out.
Preview before supervisor commit. Rows must match known data. Local uploads stay staged. We uploaded nothing here.
Twenty answers pass checks for IDs, totals, timing, routes and policy. This verifies valid answers, not accuracy.
Fraud Loop: evidence first. Every decision reviewable. Explore the queue and see why.
